title: setWindowDuration accrues under OLD rate without first pulling fresh dispatcher mint-debt, enabling owner to shorten the window and inflate the per-second emission rate against stale state
description:
`setWindowDuration` calls `_updatePool` (settling accrual under the OLD rate) but does NOT call `_syncBudget`, so any outstanding mint-debt sitting at the dispatcher hook is not pulled in before the rate is recomputed. Consequently, the new `rewardRate = rewardBudget / newDuration` is computed against a budget that may exclude substantial pending dispatcher debt. If the owner shortens the window while a large mint-debt is still at the dispatcher, the rate is set LOW (based on in-contract budget only), then a subsequent user action pulls the mint-debt and triggers another reset with `windowEnd = now + newDuration, rewardRate = fullBudget / newDuration` — using the new short duration against the freshly-swept full budget, producing a very high rate.

Also note the ordering: `windowEnd = block.timestamp + newDuration` is executed even if `totalStaked == 0`. In that case `_updatePool` only set `lastRewardTime` without accrual; subsequent stakes will begin at this aggressive rate. Combined with the absence of `whenNotPaused` on `setWindowDuration`, a pauser+owner collusion (or single-EOA admin) can pause, change the duration, and let users race to claim at an unusually high rate once unpaused.
impact: Owner can schedule an emission spike that extracts the full mint-debt over an artificially short window. Given admin-level access this is categorized as a privilege-ordering / centralization concern, but the sequencing of `_updatePool` vs `_syncBudget` is a code-level bug that makes the behavior non-obvious and breaks the invariant 'changing duration computes rate against CURRENT budget' (the current budget excludes pending dispatcher debt).
proof: Steps: (1) pool runs for months; dispatcher accumulates 10M phUSD of mint-debt; in-contract `rewardBudget` is near zero. (2) Owner calls `setWindowDuration(MIN_WINDOW = 1 days)`. `_updatePool` settles near-zero. `rewardRate = (near-zero) / 1 day ~= 0`. `windowEnd = now + 1 day`. (3) Any user calls `stake/claim`; `_syncBudget` pulls 10M phUSD; `rewardRate = 10M / 1 day` — an enormous spike. Stakers present during that 1-day window drain the whole tranche; stakers joining after windowEnd get nothing until a further pull.
recommendation: Have `setWindowDuration` call `_syncBudget` (not just `_updatePool`) so the window/rate recomputation includes any pending dispatcher mint-debt. Enforce a minimum ratio check (e.g., `rewardBudget / newDuration <= maxRate`) or a timelock on window changes. Consider gating via `whenNotPaused` too.
